skill.name: ai-automation-workflows
skill.description: Build AI automation workflows with inference.sh CLI, Bash, Python, cron scheduling, logging, retries, and webhook alerting.
skill.summary: Create reusable AI workflow templates for batch, scheduled, monitored, and multi-step automation.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms a critical remote installer piped to shell, cron-based persistence guidance, a risky dynamic command wrapper, and local file content sent to external AI services. Most other shell detections are Markdown examples or safe local substitutions rather than hidden execution. The skill needs security hardening before publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer piped directly to sh
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl pipe-to-shell install with a verified package manager flow, checksum verification, and a manual inspection step.

remediation.issue: Cron examples create persistent scheduled execution
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, document how to list and remove jobs, and recommend least-privilege service accounts.

remediation.issue: Dynamic command wrapper posts output to a webhook
remediation.suggestion: Restrict the wrapper to approved commands, redact command output, and require users to configure trusted alert destinations.

remediation.issue: Local file contents are sent to an external AI service
remediation.suggestion: Add consent, file allowlists, data classification checks, and redaction before sending file contents to model providers.

content.value_statement: AI automation often needs repeatable scripts, scheduling, retries, and monitoring. This skill provides workflow patterns for inference.sh jobs, content pipelines, and batch processing.
actual_capabilities: Provides Bash patterns for batch, sequential, parallel, conditional, and retry workflows using inference.sh CLI.
Shows cron scheduling examples for recurring content generation and report scripts.
Demonstrates logging, retry, fallback, and alert wrappers for command-line AI jobs.
Includes a Python subprocess wrapper for calling infsh app run with JSON input.
Provides templates for content calendars and text file analysis pipelines.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account and an installed infsh command.
Examples need security review before production use.
Does not manage API credentials, access controls, or secret storage.
Some templates send local or generated data to third-party AI services.

use_cases.title: Plan Content Automation
use_cases.description: Create repeatable workflows for image generation, captions, weekly themes, and scheduled publishing preparation.

use_cases.title: Process Text Files
use_cases.description: Design AI-assisted pipelines that analyze local text files and save structured summaries for review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Scheduled Jobs
use_cases.description: Draft AI job templates with retries, logging, failure alerts, and cron-based execution plans.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Batch Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-automation-workflows to design a batch image generation workflow for five product themes. Include rate limits and output naming.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scheduled Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a daily AI content job plan for my team. Include inputs, outputs, scheduling, logging, and manual review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this AI workflow for production use. Add retries, timeout guidance, failure alerts, and safe log handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-step AI pipeline for research, drafting, image generation, and social summaries. Include privacy and approval guardrails.

output_examples.input: Create a weekly content workflow for a wellness brand.
output_examples.output: A five-day plan with topics, image prompt goals, caption goals, saved outputs, and a manual approval checkpoint.

output_examples.input: Improve my AI batch job for reliability.
output: Add retries with backoff for transient failures.
Log every run with timestamps and status values.
Send alerts only after redacting command output and sensitive paths.

output_examples.input: Plan a text analysis pipeline for customer notes.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline that reads approved files, redacts sensitive data, sends prompts to an AI model, and stores reviewed summaries.

best_practices: Review every command before execution, especially installers, cron changes, and webhook calls.
Redact secrets and customer data before sending content to AI services.
Start with manual runs before enabling scheduled jobs.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installers directly into a shell.
Sending local files to external models without consent or redaction.
Creating cron jobs without logging, ownership, and cleanup guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps design AI workflows for batch generation, scheduled content, file analysis, retries, logging, and alerts.

faq.question: Does it require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples rely on the inference.sh CLI and the infsh app run command.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the examples as written?
faq.answer: No. Review installers, cron jobs, local file handling, and webhook alerts before running them.

faq.question: Does it include production security controls?
faq.answer: No. You must add credential handling, data redaction, access controls, and deployment review.

faq.question: What should I check before scheduling a workflow?
faq.answer: Confirm ownership, logging, rate limits, cleanup steps, alert destinations, and a rollback process.
